item.title: Will Jonathan Taylor, Brian Thomas Jr. get traded? How will Raiders decide on future with Maxx Crosby? What league sources are saying
item.description: With just one week left until the 2026 NFL trade deadline, texts and calls are bouncing from front office to front office. Multiple landscape-shifting trends have already materialized. The Chicago Bears’ trade of two first-round draft picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is the richest and perhaps highest-ceiling move. The New York Giants’ fifth-round pick for now-starting quarterback J.J. McCarthy may net the best value. Since the season’s start, the Houston Texans have traded for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the Dallas Cowboys have traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., the Seattle Seahawks have traded for left guard Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers have traded for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Who could be next? Yahoo Sports spoke with NFL general managers, salary-cap executives, personnel evaluators and more to take a pulse of the trade deadline landscape. All were granted anonymity due to the competitive implications of the intel. The summary: Expect more moves during the next week. But also consider the average impact of most moves (we’re not looking at you, Bears) more conservatively than initial hype may dictate. “Usually if you're looking at this time of year, a real need, you're probably not filling it,” a high-ranking NFC executive said by phone Tuesday. “You might be solidifying it. I call it, patching a leak. … You might not have planned for the Colts to be in a spiral and now their guard who is going to be a UFA, but he comes available. “Relax and just see if there's any opportunities.” An executive from a second NFC team explained they’re “always willing to make moves … if the price is right.” But how often is it? “Unless you’re paying up for this stud, do any of these deals really make sense when prices are kind of flying all over the place?” the executive told Yahoo Sports. “That, to me, is never really where the best deals get made. … But if there’s a [deal] that’s available that feels too good to be true or the other way around, you get an offer you can’t refuse? “I think obviously you have to come into that with eyes wide open.” Is Jags’ Brian Thomas Jr. ‘going to be better for the second team’? It’s easy to draw parallels between Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Houston Texans receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. That begs the question: Will any team pay for Thomas the second-round draft pick (slightly discounted with a seventh/sixth-round swap) that the Texans paid the Arizona Cardinals for Harrison? The Jaguars selected Thomas 23rd overall in the 2024 NFL Draft, 19 picks after the Cardinals selected Harrison the same year. Thomas’ career peak thus far was higher, with 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie to Harrison’s 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns the same year. Each player’s production and catch percentage have fallen since, and Houston banked on a reunion with Harrison’s college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, reviving him. Will a fresh start revive Thomas? “So

item.title: Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister
item.description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution. Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu. He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications. “I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said. Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…” When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.” He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity. “Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said. The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy. “Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said. However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements. “Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added. Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition. The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections. The post Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Raphinha, Yamal power Barca to Champions League win over Villa
item.description: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha got the goals as Barcelona beat Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday (Josep LAGO) Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. "Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar. "This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you... "From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family." Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. "Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports. "Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals." Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League. Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst. However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort. - End-to-end - Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball. Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez

item.title: Everybody is talking about Bears making Khalil Mack trade. Here’s who they must get instead
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Everybody is talking about Bears making Khalil Mack trade. Here’s who they must get instead appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears have a quarterback on a roll. And they made Jeffery Simmons a very happy man . But they might still need another piece to help with their Super Bowl assault. And while everybody is talking about the Bears making a Khalil Mack trade, here is who they must get instead. Mack, an edge rusher, would certainly add value to the Bears’ defense. However, the Bears, as they stand now, rank No. 6 in the NFL with 22 sacks. And that’s mostly without Simmons creating problems in the middle that can help things on the outside. And Bears GM Ryan Poles might be better served to add a player at the cornerback position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bears should target Chargers CB Donte Jackson There has been talk of the Bears going after Tariq Woolen. The Eagles cornerback is having a strong season. And it makes sense, in one way, to trade for a player who has good numbers on his side. However, the Bears don’t want to give up too much. This is a young roster that could be competitive for the next 3-4 years. Draft picks are valuable. And the Eagles will want a pretty penny for Woolen. Plus, Woolen’s play has trailed off some in recent seasons. And he doesn’t have a pick in eight games with six passes defended. But the best route is Jackson. He has been a solid starter in his NFL career with the Panthers, Steelers, and the last two years with the Chargers. This year, he’s played in four games with limited success. Still, Jackson brings positive things to the table, according to ESPN. “With his backfield vision and short-area closing speed, Jackson fits best as a zone corner,” Matt Bowen wrote. “He’s a top-down defender with route awareness who can create on-the-ball production. Jackson has 23 interceptions and 68 pass breakups over his career.” Those interceptions are an important part of the package. He had nine picks over the 2024 and 2025 seasons. The Bears would love a playmaker in the secondary. They have a middle-of-the-pack five interceptions so far this year. And Jackson profiles well against the run. He has a Pro Football Focus grade of 77.5 this year in a limited sample size. However, he graded out at 72.9 back in 2024. And Jackson brings a confident approach to the field, according to Chargers.com. “I feel like the last two seasons I’ve emerged, to me personally, as one of the top corners in the league,” Jackson said before the season. “That’s just kind of how I feel, so just adding to that.” And he’s a good teammate. “I’m team first, so I don’t have a personal agenda,” Jackson said. “I don’t have any personal goals but to be the best teammate I could be. item.title: Kon Knueppel Return Could Fix Hornets’ Ugly Offense
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets offense looks broken right now. They rank 30th in the NBA with a rating that trails the next worst team by 3.5 points. It is hard to watch a squad with so much shooting talent fail to score. Brandon Miller has tried to carry the load, but he cannot do it alone. The team has three wins, yet the underlying numbers show a major problem that needs fixing immediately. Hope is finally on the horizon for the Hornets. Coby White has returned to the lineup, and Kon Knueppel is close to making his season debut. Charles Lee told reporters on Monday that Knueppel’s return is imminent, even if a specific date remains unclear. “Nothing specific. He’s right behind Coby [White],” Lee stated before their home matchup versus the Detroit Pistons. The coach added that Knueppel’s return is “right around the corner,” according to DaShawn Brown writing on X. This timing could not come any sooner for a team that has struggled to put points on the board. Previous Numbers Show Explosive Potential Don’t let the current bad start fool you. The numbers from last year when White, Knueppel, and Miller played together are mind-boggling. Zach Roberts at Sports Illustrated noted that this trio posted a 134.2 offensive rating while shooting 44.7 percent from three-point range. When Miles Bridges was kept off the floor with this group, the offensive rating jumped to 147.6. These stats suggest that the Hornets offense is not beyond saving if these three can stay on the court together. Knueppel missed the first seven games of the season due to a left hamstring strain suffered in September. He has been working hard to get back in shape and recently practiced with the Greensboro Swarm. Per Yahoo Sports , ESPN’s injury report had moved his estimated return date to November 9 after he was ruled out for the Pistons game. The team assigned him to the G League for practice, a standard move for players working back from injury. His shooting prowess is exactly what this offense needs to find its rhythm again. A Trio That Changes Everything The combination of White, Knueppel, and Miller is the key to unlocking the Hornets’ potential. Last season, this group showed a net rating of +25.8 when LaMelo Ball was on the bench, proving they can generate offense on their own. Including Miles Bridges in the data set showed an even higher net rating of +37.6 when he was not on the floor. It is a tiny sample size, but the results are too good to ignore. The Hornets moved on from Ball because they felt this trio could handle the load. During the 2025-26 campaign, Knueppel posted a historic rookie year averaging 18.5 points per game while setting a new record for the most three-pointers made by a rookie. He shot 47.5 percent from the field and 42.5 percent from deep. Now that he is close to returning, the offense should see a fair margin of improvement. item.title: Lee Westwood Still Unemployed As LIV 2.0 Talks Stall
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Lee Westwood is still without a contract. The 53-year-old English star told The Chipping Forecast podcast that he is currently “unemployed” as the golf world waits for the next big move. He has not signed a deal for the revamped LIV 2.0 tour set to launch in 2027. BBC Sport reports that Westwood said the terms offered to him did not suit his needs. The league is trying to raise $300 million from BC Partners Credit to keep the project alive, but the former world No 1 remains on the sidelines. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its support last month, and the league filed for bankruptcy protection. Westwood joined LIV in 2022 when the money was flowing freely. He states now that LIV 2.0 has offered him no “anything agreeable” regarding the planned relaunch. Per Sky Sports , the details of the new format still need work before he will consider signing again. The Captaincy He Walked Away From Westwood’s path to this spot started with a choice about the Ryder Cup. He was a top pick to captain Team Europe for the 2023 event in Rome. He spoke with DP World Tour chief Guy Kinnings about the role after Whistling Straits. “It was put to me whether I’d like to be Ryder Cup captain, and I had started discussions with LIV,” Westwood said. He asked if he could still captain the team if he went to the Saudi-backed league. While Kinnings did not refuse, he indicated that the likelihood of such an outcome remained extremely low. Westwood chose the league over the trophy. He told Yahoo Sports that he had no regrets about that choice. “But we make calls in life, you make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made there.” He felt the captaincy wasn’t the be-all and end-all for him. He wanted to be in control of his own game rather than rely on others. That mindset led him to join LIV Golf in 2022, even as it cost him his spot as a future captain. A Long Road Back to the Tour Returning to the DP World Tour is not simple for Westwood. He gave up his membership when he joined LIV. If he wants to play again, he faces a 10-tournament suspension. BBC Sport reports that his return to competition cannot happen before the May tournament in Turkey. His membership is reinstated on November 12. Jon Rahm also left the series recently, citing changes to the team format he did not like. Sergio Garcia and Ian Poulter have also left LIV in recent weeks. Westwood believes the new series could succeed if costs are cut and enough players are recruited. He noted that good things can come from other people’s decisions. “Good things come out of other people’s decisions,” he told Yahoo Sports. He watched Luke Donald take over as captain and lead Team Europe to success.

item.title: PSG fly out of blocks to hit sorry Villarreal for six in Champions League
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain steamrollered Villarreal in a 6-0 Champions League demolition on Tuesday (JOSE JORDAN) Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain scored four times in the first 17 minutes on their way to a 6-0 demolition of Villarreal in Spain in the Champions League on Tuesday, as the French side shrugged off injuries to key players to maintain their perfect record in the competition this season. Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all struck at the Estadio de la Ceramica as PSG set a record for the fastest team to score four times in a match in Europe'e slite club competition. Ruiz added another early in the second half and teenager David Boly completed a comprehensive demolition of the side that finished third in La Liga last season. "I obviously wasn't expecting that but you get matches where you start in that way," PSG's Spanish coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Canal Plus. "We were impressive throughout and we are really pleased even if it is very difficult for Villarreal -- but it is hard when you play against a team like us that presses constantly." PSG have probably lost star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the campaign after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in last month's win over Barcelona, while Ousmane Dembele, captain Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are also missing just now. Despite that, the Ligue 1 leaders made it 10 straight wins in all competitions, including four in the Champions League as they aim to lift the European Cup for a third season running. They are the only team to have maximum points after four matches in this year's Champions League -- Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis all have maximum points from three games before playing on Wednesday -- and Luis Enrique's prolific side have now scored 20 goals on that run. Like all matches in the Champions League on Tuesday, a minute's silence was held prior to kick-off in tribute to Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife player who died following a collision in a Spanish second-division game on Monday. The poignant silence here was also held to remember the victims of last week's deadly train crash in Spain, in which 69 people were killed. - Record home defeat - Neves opened the scoring from close range in the ninth minute, and PSG netted three more goals in under eight minutes following that. Doue swept in as the hosts were punished for calamitous defending, and Villarreal collapsed under the intensity of PSG's pressing as Mayulu made it 3-0. Spain World Cup star Ruiz rounded off the stunning opening salvo, and the same player finished in style for 5-0 early in the second half after latching onto a ball over the top. The 17-year-old full-back Boly came on for Achraf Hakimi and almost immediately got his team's sixth goal -- his first senior strike coming on his Champions League debut. Villarreal have now lost three of their four games in Europe this season, after collecting just a single point in eight matches in last season's league phase. Mor

item.title: Steve Nash calls Kyrie Irving most skilled player ever. What does LeBron James think?
item.description: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Steve Nash calls Kyrie Irving most skilled player ever. What does LeBron James think? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving has made his long anticipated return to the court after missing the entirety of the 2025-26 season due to an ACL injury. And so far, he’s been phenomenal for the Mavericks, forming a solid one-two punch with budding star Cooper Flagg. Irving is without a doubt a future Hall of Famer, but for Steve Nash and LeBron James, the praise is greater than that. During a recent episode of the ‘Mind The Game’ Podcast, LeBron James and Steve Nash discussed Kyrie Irving’s talent, while admitting their belief that the Mavericks guard is the most-skilled player in NBA history. “I feel like Kyrie’s maybe the most, probably the most skilled player to ever play our game,” Nash said. “Just the breadth of skills, handling, shooting from all angles, finishing … he can play a long time just on that. But I think what makes him special is he’s one of the best movers … his quickness, his change of direction, deceleration, his ability to control his body air whether that’s shooting or finishing. Special, special athlete.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) James agreed with Nash’s sentiment regarding his former teammate. James and Irving won a championship together with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016 after pulling off a 3-1 comeback against the Golden State Warriors. This season, Irving has appeared in five games, at a little over 28 minutes per game. He’s averaging 21.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.2 steals with splits of 52.7 percent shooting from the field, 39 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 100 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Related: Patrick Dumont reveals plans to buy most of Mark Cuban’s remaining Mavericks shares after franchise takeover Related: Mavericks guard Max Christie exits Kings game with troubling injury

item.title: Broncos’ Bo Nix Admits He Was ‘Scared to Death’ When Patrick Mahomes Got the Ball Back in Late Drive
item.description: The Denver Broncos secured a win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but Patrick Mahomes had one final chance to change the result. That late opportunity became the focus of a postgame exchange between Mahomes and Bo Nix . Speaking to Mahomes after the game, Nix reflected on the Chiefs late fourth-quarter possession. Bo Nix shares his respect for Patrick Mahomes The Kansas City Chiefs entered the season as Super Bowl contenders , but back-to-back defeats have raised questions about their recent form. Following the Broncos’ win over the Chiefs on November 1. Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images During the postgame exchange, captured on microphone, Nix told Mahomes , “I’ve always admired you. I was scared to death when you got the ball back.” He said Mahomes’ late drive made him uneasy because of the quarterback’s history of delivering in crucial moments. The Broncos had taken a 28-24 lead with 1:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, leaving the Kansas City Chiefs with a final opportunity. Patrick Mahomes moved the offense into scoring position. Travis Kelce made a 32-yard reception during the drive, while Kenneth Walker III contributed with important runs as the Chiefs approached the Broncos goal line. The Chiefs eventually reached Denver’s 1-yard line. Mahomes appeared to complete a touchdown pass to Rashee Rice, but the play was called back because of a false start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore. Kansas City failed to score on its subsequent attempts. On fourth down, Malcolm Roach brought Mahomes down for a six-yard sack, ending the Chiefs’ final possession. Mahomes finished with 30 completions on 41 attempts for 321 passing yards and three touchdowns without an interception. He connected with Emmett Johnson for a 73-yard touchdown, while Travis Kelce finished with five receptions for 67 yards. Rice recorded seven catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Walker added 69 rushing yards on 21 attempts and 15 receiving yards. Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Jonah Coleman contributed 41 rushing yards and 63 receiving yards, including a 51-yard reception that set up Denver deep in Chiefs territory late in the fourth quarter. Coleman finished the drive with a five-yard rushing touchdown. Jaylen Waddle recorded three receptions for 39 yards and a touchdown, while Courtland Sutton added 53 receiving yards. The Broncos had trailed 24-13 before scoring 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter. Kansas City had taken a 17-13 halftime lead before Noah Gray’s four-yard touchdown reception extended its advantage in the third period. Harrison Butker also made a 45-yard field goal in the second quarter but missed a 54-yard attempt late in the fourth. Penalties proved costly for Kansas City, which was flagged 11 times for 105 yards. Denver committed

item.title: Liam Lawson Has 83 Points and Still Says ‘I Don’t Really Know What Else to Do’
item.description: Liam Lawson says he doesn’t know what else he can do to keep his Racing Bulls seat after Mexico, as Peter Bayer’s comments spark new rumors. After he was disqualified from F1 Mexico GP qualifying, Racing Bulls ’ Lawson started from the pit lane and finished seventh. He crossed the line ninth, but penalties to Oscar Piastri and Franco Colapinto moved him up. He now has 83 points and is ninth in the F1 drivers’ standings, only 24 behind Isack Hadjar, while he is comfortably ahead by 41 points of Pierre Gasly. Lawson is the best of the rest and should finish like that by the end of the 2026 season. In a normal scenario, that would be enough to seal an F1 seat. He is 45 points ahead of teammate Arvid Lindblad (38). And yet, there is no confirmation of whether the Kiwi will be retained by Racing Bulls in 2027, although PlanetF1 reports that he’s highly likely to stay, with Tsolov potentially taking a reserve role. Lawson Admits He Doesn’t Know What More to Do It is certainly draining and tiring for Lawson. Every race weekend he feels he has done enough, and still, there are no assurances. Talking to the media after Mexico, he showed first signs of being restless. “Yeah, I mean, it’s obviously a massive shame,” he said. “But it’s something that I’m just having to deal with at the moment. I’m obviously trying to do everything I can each time we get in the race car. But yeah, unfortunately, it’s just Formula One. I don’t really know what else to do, so we’ll just go out next week and try again,” summed up Lawson. It was a heavy weekend for Lawson after a clash with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in FP2, for which he apologized . The stewards gave both of them a one-place grid drop for the next race. It was also the weekend when Nikola Tsolov got his first FP1 chance. The Bulgarian F2 title contender drove Lawson’s car and finished a respectable 12th in the session, only 0.126s adrift of Lindblad. It certainly left a good impression on Racing Bulls and also Red Bull, to be a worthy contender for an F1 seat. Nikola Tsolov before his FP1 run in Mexico City. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610300440 // Usage for editorial use only // Racing Bulls Hails Tsolov’s FP1 Performance “Honestly, [Nikola’s] performance on Friday was superb,” said Racing Bulls’ CEO Bayer to Austrian TV, ORF . “It was his first time in the car, and he integrated into the team absolutely perfectly. Regarding the driver decision, he put in a fantastic performance. “That decision rests with Alan [Permane, the team principal], and he will make it, or rather, announce it, when he feels the time is right,” summed up Bayer. This was the normal answer, but what sparked fresh speculation and support for Lawson was the second answer from him. Bayer brought up the idea for which Racing Bulls is known. item.title: Ohio State football moving forward with Luke Fahey as starting quarterback
item.description: Ohio State coach Ryan Day wasn’t coy about the Buckeyes’ plans at quarterback this week. Day confirmed freshman Luke Fahey will make a second straight start behind center when the Buckeyes host Oregon on Nov. 7. While a loss at USC on Oct. 31 marked Fahey’s starting debut in place of Julian Sayin, who remains sidelined indefinitely with an injury, Day expressed confidence in Fahey moving forward. “I thought you saw him make some plays,” Day said. “He kept playing all the way to the end. I thought his attitude was good on the sideline, even though we couldn't quite get in some of the red zone opportunities. There’s things to build on for sure.” Fahey had been the Buckeyes’ backup quarterback since the start of the season, but held off sophomore Tavien St. Clair as a rare midseason competition unfolded following Sayin’s injury. Day kept their plans to start Fahey against the Trojans under wraps for most of last week. As Day reflected further on Fahey’s first start, he continued to praise the intangibles that were on display at the Los Angeles Coliseum. “He had command of the huddle,” Day said. “He showed some grit out there and toughness.” It followed feedback from teammates. “I go to the players,” Day said, “the offensive line, the wide receivers, and you say, ‘What's it like in there?’ And they were very positive about his approach out there.” Day also pointed to Fahey’s ability to extend plays. He twice scrambled to avoid the rush and gained 17 yards between the runs. Fahey finished 21 of 38 for 260 yards and one touchdown without an interception. “It was not all perfect,” Day said. “There were certainly things that happened operationally that, for a young quarterback, it was a lot on him, and he was working through it. There were some misthrows. But we expected all that to happen.” A majority of the missed throws were on deep balls. Fahey completed only two of 11 passes that traveled at least 20 yards through the air, according to Pro Football Focus. The most noticeable miss was an overthrown pass to wide receiver Devin McCuin in the second quarter. Instead of connecting with McCuin in the end zone for a 43-yard touchdown as he blew past the coverage, the ball sailed out of bounds. Fahey went deep to star receiver Jeremiah Smith three times, but they connected only once for 27 yards. Each of Smith’s previous games with double-digit catches this season against Illinois and Iowa saw him finish with more than 200 receiving yards, but he had just 83 yards with his 10 catches last week. The missed shots left Fahey with an average of 6.8 yards per attempt against the Trojans. It was a drop-off from the 10.5 yards per attempt that Sayin had averaged during the first seven games, though not uncharacteristic for a first-time starting quarterback. When Sayin made his debut as a redshirt freshman last season against Texas, he averaged 6.3 yards per pass attempt and posted lower marks later in 2025 against Illinois (6.1) and UCLA (5.9). item.title: The Bears’ Big Trade May Have Unlocked Something Else
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears paid a substantial price for Jeffery Simmons because they needed someone who could change games from the middle of their defensive line. His first appearance offered an encouraging possibility: the trade could also help them get more from another expensive investment. Montez Sweat returned from his two-game suspension Monday night and immediately gave Seattle problems. He finished Chicago’s 34-17 victory with a sack, three quarterback hits and a tackle for loss. Two additional sacks were erased by defensive holding penalties. Afterward, Simmons revealed that he had arrived with a challenge for his former Mississippi State teammate. “I challenged him this week,” Simmons said during his postgame press conference . “Get back to the old Sweat.” Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears defensive line Montez Sweat (98) reacts after a sack against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images That request carried some history. Simmons knew Sweat long before either player joined the Bears. Their reunion gave him a chance to demand the version of his teammate he remembered from college, and their first game together provided reasons to believe the partnership could work. Sweat entered Monday needing a productive return . He had two sacks through five appearances before serving a suspension for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing substances policy. Chicago won both games he missed, beating Atlanta and New England. The Bears had committed heavily to Sweat after acquiring him in 2023, signing him to a four-year, $98 million extension. His ability to affect quarterbacks remained important to their ambitions, even as attention shifted toward the All-Pro arriving from Tennessee. Simmons’ presence gave Sweat a different set of opportunities. “I definitely got my opportunities,” Sweat told The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain . “I definitely had some one-on-ones. I was looking forward to taking advantage of it, so I’m looking forward to doing that for the rest of the year.” Those individual matchups are a significant part of the appeal. An offense that devotes extra help to Simmons has fewer resources available elsewhere. Pressure through the middle can also reduce the space a quarterback has to step away from a defender coming around the edge. Sweat still has to defeat the blocker in front of him. In Seattle, he repeatedly did enough to disrupt Sam Darnold, including on the two sacks that penalties wiped away. Those plays cannot be added to his official total, but they belong in an assessment of how he performed. Chicago saw more successful rushes than the final sack column alone would suggest. The benefits also reached defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. According to Fishbain’s reporting, the Bears posted their lowest blitz rate of the season at 20.5 percent while generating 14 pressures. item.title: FC Barcelona’s $721M fan spending estimate puts it ahead of its rivals
item.description: FC Barcelona’s $721M fan spending estimate puts it ahead of its rivals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . FC Barcelona had more in common with the NFL and Major League Baseball than with its closest soccer rivals in Zero1 Gaming’s October 2026 fan spending report . The study put Barcelona sixth among 45 fandoms, with an estimated $721.28 million in spending. The NFL and MLB were the only sports entries ahead of it. Manchester United and Real Madrid finished seventh and eighth, respectively, leaving Barcelona as the highest-ranked individual team in the study. Sixth place sounds less impressive until you look at the company. Pokémon finished first at an estimated $1.71 billion, and the NFL came second at $1.36 billion. Disney and Super Mario followed before MLB rounded out the top five. Barcelona was the first individual club on a list that, to that point, had been led by entire leagues and entertainment franchises. Its position is striking because the study puts one club’s shopping demand on the same scale as all of those different kinds of fandom. 🚨🇧🇷| RECORD: Raphinha (29) is now Barcelona's 4TH-HIGHEST GOALSCORER in UEFA Champions League history! ✅ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He has 23 goals, overtaking Neymar Jr. ⚽️🔝 pic.twitter.com/Rrrys4AAKu — Kalshi FC (@KalshiFC) November 3, 2026 Barcelona’s edge starts with what fans searched for Zero1 Gaming put Manchester United at $562.31 million and Real Madrid at $558.69 million. That leaves Barcelona about $159 million clear of United and $163 million ahead of Madrid in the model. The gaps are especially interesting because the study used the same price for each club’s signature item, a $100 replica jersey. Barcelona had the advantage before the model put a dollar value on any of those searches. The club drew 12.32 million purchase-related searches in the study’s September 2026 data. Real Madrid drew 9.68 million, and Manchester United drew 9.63 million. Barcelona’s lead of more than 2.6 million searches over either club matters because the model applies the same purchase assumptions to each fandom. With the jersey price held constant, a bigger pool of searches produces a bigger estimate for that part of the calculation. The report gives signature products more weight than any other purchase category. It assumes a 35% conversion rate for those products, compared with 17.5% for apparel, 5% for premium collectibles, and 1.25% for tickets. Across all 45 fandoms, signature items represented almost half of estimated spending. A jersey serves that role for a soccer club, just as a game can for a gaming franchise. That shared framework helps explain how Barcelona and Super Mario can occupy places on the same list. There’s also a reason the jersey makes sense as the centerpiece of a sports fandom. As a Zero1 Gaming expert put it, “A jersey, a trading card, or a plush toy works like a membership badge, and fans are happy to pay for it wh

item.title: Cristante: “We cannot allow these comebacks. We need to revisit our mistakes.”
item.description: Cristante: “We cannot allow these comebacks. We need to revisit our mistakes.” Bryan Cristante spoke to Sky Sport after the defeat against Manchester United. “We came in well, we played a great first half that could have ended even more than 2-0. Then there are the opponents, who are strong and when they push forward and find the right moment, they become difficult to contain.” “We had to do something more, especially because we’d been through it before. That penalty… I didn’t watch it again, but from the pitch it looked very dubious.” “When they get going, they’re strong players and difficult to contain. We need to take a good look at it and understand where we’re going wrong; it’s becoming a bit too frequent.” “We definitely need to be more focused at the back, the whole team. We were 2-0 up, and every now and then we can drop back and keep the game going, letting the others play, but without conceding goals. We need to revisit it and understand where we went wrong.” “We played a great half, against a strong team despite not being in their best form, and in a stadium like this. We need to take the positives, but we know this is a point and we need to improve. We will do it, we need to understand where we went wrong so we don’t make these mistakes again.”

item.title: Yankees Need To Try Trading For This Brewers All-Star
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill The New York Yankees extended a qualifying offer to David Bednar, but it's extremely unlikely that he will accept it. While that does not mean that the Yankees won't find a way to bring him back, it does mean the Yankees need to be ready to replace him if he does leave. Bednar is one of the best relievers in the game and has been great ever since the Yankees acquired him. Last season, he posted a 2.47 ERA and recorded 35 saves. If he leaves, the Yankees will need to find a new closer, and while they could try to do so in free agency, trading for a closer may be the right move. The Milwaukee Brewers are reportedly open to trading All-Star closer Trevor Megill, and the Yankees should try to get him. Megill has one more season before free agency, just like Devin Williams did when the Yankees acquired him. Williams did not work out in the Bronx, but Megill seems more built for the pressure that comes with playing in New York. Unlike Williams, he shined in the postseason, showing pressure does not bother him. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Megill was integral in the Brewers' success this season, but history suggests the Brewers will find a way to trade him this offseason, handing the keys to the ninth inning to Abner Uribe. Not only would Megill replace Bednar, but there's an argument to be made that he's better. He is a National League Reliever of the Year finalist this season and has been lights-out in the biggest moments. item.title: Kuyt: “Everyone Knows How Much Fenerbahce and Liverpool Mean to Me”
item.description: Liverpool’s league phase Champions League tie against Fenerbahce on Wednesday is a chance for the Reds to push to a perfect 4-0 in Europe’s premier cup competition. And it’s a chance to maybe work out a few of their frustrations following Sunday’s referee-assisted 1-0 defeat to Arsenal. It’s also a reunion with a cult legend at the club, with Dirk Kuyt having recently taken over as interim manager following the recent dismissal of İsmail Kartal. Kuyt played 130 games for the Turkish club after the forward joined them from Liverpool in 2012 after six seasons and 285 games in Red, and after moving into management with spells at clubs in Holland and Belgium, he signed on to be Kartal’s assistant at Fenerbahce back in June. Now, he’s coming up against Liverpool. “First of all, it’s a really special achievement to be in the Champions League for the first time in 18 years with Fenerbahce,” Kuyt said today at his pre-match press conference when asked about coming up against the club he played more games for as a player than any other. “That was something really exciting and you always know you’re going to play against exciting teams. But as soon as the draw came up, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me. From that moment, I knew it was going be a special occasion for me. “But at the stage we are, I’m not important person—it’s the club. The fans deserve much more, they deserve a good performance. We have good players but we need to show up with good energy, with passion, and to play—and then I think it can be a very special night.” Special, though, doesn’t mean he’s hoping for any result other than a win for his side, who currently sit sixth in the Turkish Super Lig—but 31st out of the 36 sides in the Champions League with just two points to show for their opening four league phase matches and their knockout hopes now quickly fading. “Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce,” Kuyt added. “If the fans will show up, too, I think Europe will see how big this club is.”

item.title: Alex Caruso to return from 3-game absence in OKC's game against Cavaliers
item.description: Help has arrived. The Oklahoma City Thunder will have Alex Caruso available for Wednesday's game against the Cleveland Cavaliers . He had missed the last three games with an ankle sprain. Since the last time Caruso played, the Thunder have received even grimmer injury news. Chet Holmgren will miss two-plus months with a small torn patellar tendon. He underwent a biological treatment to recover from it. That means he'll be out until around New Year's. Of course, there's also the long-term absences of Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. The Thunder are in a new NBA reality. Williams sustained a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle. Wallace sustained a torn labrum. Both had surgery to fix the problems. Their 2026-27 season status is up in the air and will be re-evaluated before the 2027 NBA playoffs start. But the Thunder can worry about all of that another day. For now, Caruso's return is much needed. He's expected to take on a bulkier load with the large number of absences. The 32-year-old has been off to a stellar start. He's averaged 9.3 points on 56.5% shooting, 4.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists in four games this season. Remains to be seen if Caruso starts, but he'll surely take on either Donovan Mitchell or James Harden as the Thunder and Cavaliers wrap up their regular-season series. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Alex Caruso to return from 3-game absence in OKC's game against Cavaliers

item.title: 'We don't need to save anyone's job,' says Man Utd captain Fernandes
item.description: Bruno Fernandes' penalty sparked Manchester United's second-half revival against Roma [Getty Images] Bruno Fernandes says Manchester United's players "don't need to save anyone's job" after their improbable comeback win against Roma in the Champions League. The Red Devils produced a remarkable second-half fightback to come from 2-0 down to win 3-2 and end a run of nine games without a victory. Fernandes was speaking to the media for the first time since being dropped to the bench after publicly criticising manager Michael Carrick's tactics in the wake of their 4-1 loss at Como. Restored to the team for the Premier League defeat by Chelsea, the 32-year-old's penalty on 58 minutes sparked an incredible revival to ease some of the pressure on Carrick. But when asked if the result would save his job, United captain Fernandes told Amazon Prime: "We don't need to save anyone's job." He continued: "The club needed that win, the players needed that win. We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. "It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air, then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I'm not performing. "Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. "It doesn't change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me." More to follow. item.title: Lightning’s Kucherov Crisis About More Than Money
item.description: David Zalubowski/AP The Tampa Bay Lightning have spent the better part of a decade building a championship-caliber roster around Nikita Kucherov. Now, the franchise’s most productive player is questioning whether the organization deserves to keep him. Saturday, he firmly requested a trade following a face-to-face meeting with general manager Julien BriseBois, and his blunt comments Monday indicated the Lightning may have burned the bridge with their reigning Hart Trophy winner. Kucherov’s trade request has largely been framed as a contract dispute, but he insisted money was never the issue. Instead, Kucherov pointed to what he describes as a breakdown in communication and respect between himself and the GM, claiming that the two have spoken only twice in the last four months. However, it should be noted that BriseBois immediately responded to Kucherov’s request with an equally firm public statement that the Lightning would not trade him. For an organization that has built its identity around winning and star players, the current quagmire is significant. If they can reel back the situations, the Lightning may ultimately face a difficult decision over how much to pay Kucherov. But before they can resolve the financial implications of their inaction, they must confront a more immediate question: How did they allow negotiations with their most indispensable player to reach this point? According to Kucherov, 33, the breakdown was not for lack of opportunity. Reports indicated that the Lightning initially offered the winger a four-year extension carrying a $13 million average annual value in July, followed by a six-year offer at a $15 million AAV in September. Neither proposal was enough to secure his commitment, certainly not in light of Leo Carlsson’s $18 million AAV offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers, and the gaggle of players whose salaries are now in that range. With Kucherov’s camp reportedly seeking a six-year deal closer to $20 million annually, the financial gap between the two sides is considerable. But the player’s account suggests that the numbers alone do not explain the impasse. Two conversations in four months is a strikingly small amount of engagement for a player of Kucherov’s stature. The 33-year-old has established himself as one of the most prolific offensive players of his generation, winning two Hart Trophies and three Art Ross Trophies while just recently becoming the Lightning’s all-time leading scorer. His contributions have been instrumental to the franchise’s sustained success, including its consecutive Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021. For a player who has given so much to the organization, the apparent lack of urgency surrounding his future raises legitimate questions about the front office’s priorities. BriseBois has earned considerable credibility for his ability to construct and maintain a championship-caliber roster. One of the defining characteristics of his tenure has been the Lightning’s ability to re

item.title: Bayern skeleton crew sink Atletico in Champions League
item.description: Bayern Munich celebrate after their second goal in Tuesday's win at Atletico Madrid. (Oscar DEL POZO) Bayern Munich overcame a horror list of absences to cruise to a 2-0 win away at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday. Teenage Germany forward Lennart Karl opened the scoring and Konrad Laimer added another as Bayern triumphed despite a bulging casualty ward. Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari were on Bayern's injury list but it meant little as freshly-minted Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane and captain Joshua Kimmich marshalled his troops to a memorable victory. The German champions also arrived in Madrid without coach Vincent Kompany, sick with a meningitis-related condition. "There was a lot of noise around us heading in but we're very convinced of the squad we have, of the players we've got at our disposal and I think we showed over 90 minutes the type of football we can play," Laimer, who was named man of the match by UEFA, told Amazon Prime. "We could've scored another goal or two. It was a very deserved win against a good team and an important three points." Despite laying on an assist for Laimer, Kane failed to score meaning he missed out on equalling Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in 11 straight Champions League games. "We are standing together despite the difficult times at Bayern in the last weeks and are delighted we could experience this team victory together," Bayern captain Manuel Neuer said. "We heard that people were doubting how well we could perform today against a top team, just two points behind Barcelona in La Liga, but to give an answer in the way we did is sensational." - Atletico's 'cold shower' - Atletico's Marcos Llorente told Movistar+ the hosts were stunned by Bayern's opener. "They're a strong side but we were holding our own. It's the little details that decide a game, and we weren't expecting that first goal. "We were covering well, so it hit us like a bucket of cold water." With two wins and two draws, Bayern climbed to eighth spot on the table while Atletico finish Tuesday night in 22nd spot on the 36-team table. Undermanned Bayern were handed a boost pre-match when Michael Olise was given the all clear to start after being subbed out late with a knee injury against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday. Olise joined Bayern's two remaining senior forwards Kane and Karl in the starting line-up, with wingback Alphonso Davies pushed up onto the left wing. Atletico were received their own late injury withdrawal when Christian Romero was ruled out on matchday. Julian Alvarez came close to giving the hosts an early lead, flashing inches wide of the post three minutes in. Kane had his own chance to break the deadlock midway through the opening half but blasted wide of Jan Oblak's goal on the turn. Atletico had repelled the visitors despite ceding possession and field position but it was a simple mistake from the hosts which allowed Bayern to take the lead. Robin Le Normand took too long

item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. Latest Beavers news Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout Atkinson, Legree join Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. He is definitely a threat in coverage and in the pass game.” Oregon State (1-2) at UTEP (1-2) When: Saturday, Sept. 26 Time: 6 p.m. PT Where: Sun Bowl, El Paso, Texas Betting line: Oregon State by 10.5 TV: MW+ (Mountain West Plus) On air: KEX 1190 in Portland, KEJO 1240 and 93.7 in Corvallis Stream : You c

item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. item.title: Cade Cunningham’s 33-Point Surge Turns Hornets Home Game Into A Blowout
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The final score of 124-91 looks like a standard win, but the real story is how the Pistons took control before the third quarter even ended. Cade Cunningham scored a season-high 33 points on Monday night in Charlotte, N.C., yet he did not even play in the fourth quarter, according to CT Insider . This means the Hornets had already lost the game by the time the final period started. The Associated Press noted that in only three quarters, Cunningham hit 13 of 20 shots while contributing five rebounds, five steals, and seven assists. The young Hornets squad posted a 45-16 run in the third quarter. Reporting for Detroit Bad Boys indicated that 14 of Cunningham’s points came in fewer than three and a half minutes of playing time. Taking full responsibility for the team, he stated “We’re playing too well to not blow these guys out.” The Pistons extended their lead to 29 points when Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter hit back-to-back threes. The Third Quarter Collapse By the end of the third quarter, the Pistons held a 98-75 lead after starting with an 11-point halftime advantage. The Hornets coach, Charles Lee, decided to empty his bench early because the result was no longer in doubt. Brandon Miller finished with 17 points for Charlotte, while Naz Reid added 13, but it was not enough to stop the surge. Defending against such efficiency proved difficult as the Pistons made 57% of their floor attempts and 48% from deep. With less than five minutes remaining in the second quarter, Dennis Schroder scored a layup to maintain a two-possession lead, yet the Hornets never returned to contention after that. The Pistons made 13 of their first 24 three-point attempts, setting a tone that the Hornets could not match. This performance marks the Pistons’ third straight win, showing a team that is finding its rhythm at the perfect time. Shooting Numbers Tell the Story The Detroit Bad Boys’ shooting stats are shown. At a certain stage of the game, the Pistons were converting more than 60% of their shots from the floor and 50% from three-point range. Duncan Robinson added 24 points behind six 3-pointers, giving the Hornets a hard time on the perimeter. When 1:17 remained in the third quarter, Cunningham headed to the bench, indicating the coach believed the outcome was settled. This decision allowed the starters to rest while the reserves played out the final minutes. Hornets fans in the arena saw the game become a blowout faster than expected.

item.title: Matheus Cunha in tense exchange of words with Michael Carrick after Man United's dramatic win
item.description: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick and Matheus Cunha exchanged words post-game on Tuesday -Credit:Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images Matheus Cunha and Michael Carrick appeared to exchange words following Manchester United's thrilling victory over AS Roma. Cunha was the standout performer for the Reds as two late goals in three minutes secured a 3-2 win against the Italian side in the UEFA Champions League. After the Brazilian netted the winner, he removed his shirt and leapt into the celebrating United supporters, earning himself a yellow card in the process. Shortly afterward, he collected a second yellow and a resulting red for a late challenge on a Roma player. When the final whistle sounded, Cunha moved to join the post-match celebrations, but was promptly intercepted by Carrick. Following their brief exchange, the former Wolverhampton Wanderers forward appeared visibly upset before making his way toward the Old Trafford tunnel, as per the Manchester Evening News . Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Goalkeeper involved in tragic Jesús de Miguel collision 'breaks down' after soccer star's death -Credit:Simon Stacpoole/Offside, Offside via Getty Images The reason behind the Brazilian's apparent frustration following his short conversation with the United manager remains unclear. Nevertheless, Cunha made a point of stopping to acknowledge the elated home supporters before disappearing down the tunnel. While the exact nature of the exchange between Carrick and Cunha remains unknown, it is possible the United boss urged the Brazilian to return to the locker room to avoid any additional sanctions. Players dismissed from the field are typically required to remain in the locker room until the match officials have vacated the pitch. Under IFAB Law 12 (Fouls and Misconduct), a red-carded player who enters the field immediately after the final whistle, whether to celebrate with teammates or confront officials, can be classified as an unauthorized pitch entry and misconduct. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Regardless, it will not dampen United's spirits, following a dismal stretch of results. United were lackluster in the opening 45 minutes and were deservedly trailing 2-0 at the break, after Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen gave the Serie A club a 2-0 advantage.

item.title: “It was right”: Bruno Fernandes acknowledges his error and backs Michael Carrick after special Champions League comeback
item.description: “It was right”: Bruno Fernandes acknowledges his error and backs Michael Carrick after special Champions League comeback Manchester United produced another Champions League comeback for the ages as they came back from two goals down to beat AS Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday. It was the Matheus Cunha show as the Brazilian won the penalty before grabbing a brace to turn the match on its head. The way the players pressed and counter-attacked at times was a callback to the United of old, and Michael Carrick must utilise this blueprint against Aston Villa next to potentially save his job. It was Bruno Fernandes who kickstarted the comeback with his second penalty after he had missed the initial one. Bruno Fernandes kickstarted United’s comeback Thankfully, the referee had spotted an encroachment that allowed the Portuguese superstar another bite at the cherry. The club captain has been under pressure following his outburst against the head coach before he was dropped against Bournemouth. There have been reports of the pair clearing the air , and now the Portugal international must start delivering on the pitch. He spoke to the broadcasters after the match and took responsibility for his poor recent displays and his public criticism, while vowing to keep at it to change the club’s fortunes. Club captain acknowledges his error “It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened. “The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn’t performing. And that’s fair. Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right. “The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club. And it doesn’t change my aim to win every f—king game that I have ahead of me.” Backing for Carrick The attacking midfielder was asked whether the team were trying to save Carrick’s job, and Bruno Fernandes made it clear that everyone needed that result, including the players and the staff. “We don’t need to save anyone’s job. The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff. We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together.” Feature image Michael Regan via Getty Images

item.title: 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A fresh supremacy battle has erupted in the Benue State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, following the rejection of about 500-man campaign council for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia by the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, a political mobilisation platform associated with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume. The disagreement followed Monday’s announcement by the APC State Organising Secretary, James Ornguga, of a joint campaign council for Tinubu and Alia ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also fixed Thursday, November 5, for the inauguration of the council in Makurdi, with a supplementary list expected to be released later. However, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, in a disclaimer issued Tuesday and signed by its Director-General, Chief Akange Audu, disowned the purported campaign structure, alleging that the names of its conveners, members and political candidates had been included without their authorisation. The Alliance specifically faulted the inclusion of its conveners, Senator Jack Tilley-Gyado, and Elder Simon Shango, as well as its candidates for the National Assembly and Benue State House of Assembly, in the list of the purported Alia campaign council. It stated, “for the avoidance of doubt, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 categorically dissociates itself from the said publication and disowns any claim or suggestion that the individuals mentioned therein are associated with, or constitute members of, the purported Alia Campaign structure.” The group further questioned the political arrangement that reportedly placed Governor Alia as chairman of the campaign council while listing Akume, whom it described as the founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, as merely a member. According to the Alliance, “We find it particularly contentious that a purported Alia Campaign structure would designate Governor Hyacinth Alia as its Chairman while listing the Founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, Sen. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.” The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. This has contributed to the divisions and disagreements currently affecting the party in the state.” Despite rejecting the campaign council, the group insisted that “the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 remains committed to its stated mandate of mobilising support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “Our political engagement also extends to supporting APC candidates for the National Assembly and the Benue State House of Assembly who emerge from the list and leadership direction recognised by our leader, Sen. George Akume.” The Alliance al

item.title: Rising feed costs threaten poultry, livestock farming in 3 states
item.description: Farmers in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states have warned that rising feed costs, expensive day-old chicks and poor market prices threaten livestock production and livelihoods. They said the situation had forced some operators to reduce production, sell their animals at losses or abandon farming altogether. The farmers spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday during a nationwide survey in Minna. They identified high feed costs, which account for 70 to 80 per cent of poultry production expenses, as their biggest challenge. They called for subsidised feed ingredients, affordable financing, improved access to essential inputs and local feed mills to reduce production costs. In Kogi, a poultry farmer and retired Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security director, Mr Dare Olukaiyeja, said feeding accounted for 80 per cent of his production costs. Olukaiyeja, who keeps 250 birds, said a crate of eggs currently sold for about N6,200 amid declining consumer purchasing power. Similarly, Mr Shola Adeyi, a Lokoja-based farmer with a 1,000-bird capacity, said feed prices had increased by N2,000 to N3,000 per bag almost monthly since January. He said starter, finisher and layer feeds sold for N22,500, N22,000 and N16,000 respectively, while day-old chicks cost about N2,200 each. Adeyi identified unreliable electricity, extreme heat and high bird mortality as additional challenges confronting poultry farmers. He said some operators had abandoned the business because they could not afford alternative power sources. He said eggs sold for between N6,000 and N6,500 per crate, while broilers fetched N4,500 to N5,000 per kilogramme. According to him, the prices barely covered production costs, necessitating long-term subsidised or interest-free loans and effective market regulation. Another farmer, Mr Malik Ajayi, said day-old chick and feed prices usually increased during Sallah, Easter and Christmas. Ajayi, who rears broilers, cockerels and foreign turkeys, said he recently bought three cartons of day-old chicks for N352,500. He attributed some price fluctuations to possible exploitation by large-scale producers and urged the government to introduce effective price regulation. Ajayi, who keeps 150 broilers, 50 cockerels and 15 foreign turkeys, said some farmers sold their birds cheaply to avoid prolonged feeding costs. He added that frozen poultry dealers also faced high electricity and preservation expenses. Mrs Oluwaseyi Fadaka, another Lokoja-based farmer, said a bag of feed now cost about N22,000, with her 40 Noiler birds consuming one regularly. She said rising feeding costs were eroding profits, forcing farmers to sell at losses or abandon the business. Fadaka said some smallholders were exploring organic feeding alternatives but needed government support through subsidised feed and affordable, quality inputs. JP Morgan’s Nigeria expansion to boost foreign investment — IMPI
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Independent Media and Policy Initiative (IMPI) has said the planned expansion of global financial giant JP Morgan Chase into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector could attract fresh foreign investments, improve corporate financing and strengthen the country’s access to international capital markets. The policy think tank said the American financial institution’s application for a national merchant banking licence was a significant endorsement of Nigeria’s investment prospects and could encourage more multinational corporations to commit long-term capital to the country. In a policy statement signed by its Chairman, Dr Omoniyi Akinsiju, IMPI said the proposed expansion could reshape Nigeria’s corporate finance landscape by making it easier for businesses to access funding, structure large-scale projects and manage risks associated with cross-border investments. According to the group, JP Morgan’s transition from a representative office to a fully licensed merchant bank would enable it to deepen its involvement in trade finance, corporate lending, cross-border underwriting and other sophisticated financial transactions. It said the development could be particularly beneficial to capital-intensive sectors such as energy, telecommunications and manufacturing, where high borrowing costs and complex financing arrangements had continued to constrain investments. “JP Morgan Chase’s move to secure a national merchant banking licence in Nigeria marks a significant shift in West Africa’s corporate finance landscape,” IMPI said. The group added that the proposed operations could help multinational companies structure investments more efficiently through direct access to cross-border trade facilities, commodity hedging instruments and syndicated financing involving domestic and international markets. It said the availability of such services could reduce delays and additional costs businesses often encounter when relying on multiple financial intermediaries to execute major projects. IMPI also argued that Nigeria’s sovereign and corporate borrowers could benefit from stronger links to international capital markets, while the presence of a major global financial institution could reinforce confidence among foreign pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and private equity investors. However, the think tank cautioned that JP Morgan’s proposed entry would not automatically translate into increased foreign direct investment, stressing that the broader benefits would depend on prevailing investment conditions and the consistency of economic policies. Tinubu’s reforms and investor confidence The policy group attributed renewed international interest in Nigeria to the economic policy direction of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly the foreign exchange market reforms and removal of petrol subsidy introduced in 2023. item.title: Champions League: Man United rise from the dust to shock Roma 3-2
item.description: Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford. The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. But Matheus Cunha’s struck twice after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had given United hope to end a nine-game winless run in all competitions. The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of previous trips to Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini’s lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. The Italians have now lost on all five visits to the Theatre of Dreams, most notably when Carrick scored twice in a 7-1 thrashing in the Champions League quarter-finals 19 years ago. Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez’s foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora’s pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Soule’s shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. Malen converted the resulting penalty for his 12th goal of the season. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United’s unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick’s luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes’s first spot-kick was saved by Roma’s third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts and Roma captain Bryan Cristante had to hack clear off the line as the visitors rode their luck. However, Leonardo Balerdi’s swipe at fresh air deep inside his own box gifted Cunha the simplest task to tap in an equaliser seven minutes from time. Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration. Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time. The 10 men held on to breathe new life into United’s Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats
